chunks: And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who married two sisters in a single contract, he said: “He keeps whichever of the two he wishes and lets the other go.”
And he said regarding a man who married five women in a single contract: “He lets go whichever of them he wishes.”

key_terms.يُمْسِكُ: he keeps or retains in marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries two sisters or five women in a single marriage contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about invalid excess in a marriage contract. If a man contracts marriage with two sisters together, he may retain one and release the other; and if he marries five women in one contract, he must release whichever one he chooses so that only four remain.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4460 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a man who married two sisters in a single contract.
Imam (as) said: "He should keep whichever one he wishes and release the other."

And regarding a man who married five women in a single contract.
Imam (as) said: "He should release whichever ones he wishes."
